inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: The Taoiseach was in Limerick bragging about housing tenancies rising even after his government forced those March 1 rules on landlords for six-year leases. He dismissed the obvious spike in eviction notices and homelessness, but the number of people in emergency accommodation has gone up again across the nation. This is exactly what happens when government interferes too much in private rental agreements, attacking property rights and family stability. We must get back to personal responsibility and market signals to maintain order instead of letting bureaucrats tear down the foundations of our stable society.
